items.title: 5 Fantasy Football Bold Predictions - Aidin Ebrahimi's Week 12 Picks (2026)
Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said he’s “not sure yet” if Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) will play in Week 12 against the Titans.
items.text: Fantasy managers don’t need to panic just yet. The Jaguars have not taken the field for their Friday practice, and Coen said the team will assess how he looks on Friday before making any further decisions on his availability. Tuten has not practiced in either of the first two practices of the week, so a limited practice would be a slight upgrade for him heading into the weekend. We will check back in with a final update on his availability when the team announces it, but backup Chris Rodriguez could be in line for a busy week if Tuten were to be sidelined. - Zachary Krueger

items.title: Parker Washington (shoulder) will not play in the Jaguars’ Week 12 game against the Titans.
items.text: According to head coach Liam Coen, Washington aggravated an AC joint injury in Thursday’s practice that will sideline him for at least one week. Speaking with the media on Friday, Coen said the team hopes to have him back “ASAP” but noted that it is a “week-to-week injury.” Jakobi Meyers could be first in line to benefit from Washington’s absence, but this certainly isn’t an ideal situation for fantasy managers with the fantasy playoffs just weeks away. - Zachary Krueger

items.title: Dallas Goedert (shoulder) was spotted in a sling after the Eagles’ Week 12 win over the Cowboys.
items.text: Goedert exited Week 12’s win over the Cowboys with a shoulder injury on the first drive of the game. The veteran tight end did not return to the game, and the fact that he was wearing a sling after the game suggests this could be somewhat of a serious injury. Head coach Nick Sirianni did not comment on his injury after the game, so it’s possible we won’t learn until later next week what he’s dealing with and how much time he could miss, if any. items.title: Rashee Rice caught 2-of-5 targets for 19 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills.
items.text: Rice’s quiet day was made all the worse by the refs when they overturned his third catch to an incomplete pass after replay showed the ball hitting the ground. While the tip of the ball did touch the turf, the ball didn’t appear to move. While the controversial call eventually led to a Buffalo victory, calling it a catch would have changed little for fantasy managers. Rice has played five games since returning from his early-season hamstring injury. He had more than 53 yards in just one of them. items.title: Travis Kelce caught 4-of-7 targets for 71 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills.
items.text: Kelce was the only member of the Chiefs’ passing attack to find any success in this game. Being battered by the elements, Patrick Mahomes relied on his trusted tight end for a handful of big plays throughout the contest. One of them was a 21-yard toss to the nine-yard line at the end of the first half that set up a short field goal. Kelce, however, paid the price with a helmet to the back that left him on the ground in pain for a while. He ultimately played through the issue, though we expect to see him on the injury report next week. Kelce, unfortunately, did not go out on a high note, droppi

items.title: Ty Johnson caught both of his targets for 12 yards in the Bills’ Week 12 win over the Chiefs.
items.text: Johnson spiked for 55 yards on seven catches last week. That usage was nowhere to be found on Thanksgiving. It was a rain-soaked rock-fight of a game in which the Bills barely even tried to pass. Josh Allen threw the ball 21 times and only 10 were caught. The low volume axed any chance Johnson had of an encore. Facing a lowly Patriots team in Week 13, we don’t expect much work for Buffalo’s third-down back next week. Johnson will be buried in the RB5 ranks. - Kyle Dvorchak

items.title: Khalil Shakir caught 3-of-6 targets for 33 yards in the Bills’ Week 12 win over the Chiefs.
items.text: Shakir led the Bills in targets, catches, and yards, but it was a memorable Thanksgiving for the worst kind of reason. Josh Allen tossed him a simple screen pass in the red zone late in the third quarter, but Shakir failed to corral the ball and bobbled it right into the hands of Chiefs corner Nohl Williams. The good news for Shakir is that the blunder didn’t land him in the doghouse. Allen’s very next attempt went to Shakir for a six-yard gain. Shakir has been a steady option out of the slot this year, but the spike weeks have been nonexistent. He has one touchdown and a single 100-yard game

items.title: Josh Downs caught 1-of-4 targets for 13 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills.
items.text: This was by far Downs’ quietest game as a Chief, though his second half special teams play was rather loud. Downs made a pair of questionable decisions on fourth quarter punts, twice fielding the ball near the Chiefs’ own goal line. Neither gamble came close to working. The only good news was Downs did not cough the ball up. Downs’ snaps once again didn’t really kick up on offense, as he was on the field for just 16 plays. Perhaps that will finally, finally change in Week 13 against the Rams. For now, Downs is a boom/bust WR3 in fantasy football. - Patrick Daugherty

items.title: Xavier Worthy was held without a catch on three targets in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills.
items.text: It was a rainy, wind-swept night in Buffalo, but Patrick Mahomes still managed to have a decent evening. The same was not true for his former No. 2 receiver, who “zero balled” even as also-rans like Cyrus Allen and Jalen Royals caught passes. Held to just two catches in three games since Josh Downs’ Kansas City arrival, Worthy is turning into a tough hold even in 14-team leagues. - Patrick Daugherty

items.title: Dalton Kincaid caught 2-of-2 targets for 13 yards in the Bills’ Week 12 win over the Chiefs.
items.text: Two catches looks bad until you realize Josh Allen completed only 10 throws in a rain-marred affair. It’s still sadly unsurprising Kincaid was one of the biggest victims of a run-heavy game environment. Rather amazingly, tonight was the fifth time in 10 2026 appearances Kincaid was held to three-or-fewer targets. He’s becoming more of a fringe TE1 than locked-in option, though the return of byes for Week 13 means he will probably still crack the top 12 against the Patriots. - Patrick Daugherty
